title: The cognitive-motor link, certified: slower processing speed tracks more postural sway (Kendall's tau-b bit-for-bit vs scipy.stats.kendalltau and base R)

dataset.name: BDS -- a public data set of human balance evaluations (Santos & Duarte 2016)
dataset.record: per subject: Trail Making Test part A time (s) + eyes-closed-foam COP path length (cm); n=158
dataset.citation: Santos DA, Duarte M. A public data set of human balance evaluations. PeerJ 2016;4:e2648. doi:10.7717/peerj.2648.

proposition: Postural control draws on attention and executive function -- the cognitive-motor link. In the BDS cohort (n=158), slower Trail Making Test A time (worse processing speed) is associated with more eyes-closed-foam sway. Each subject's sway comes from the certified swayMetrics; the NEWLY-AUTHORED kendallTau -- Kendall's tau-b, the concordance-based rank correlation (the third method after Pearson's r and Spearman's rho) -- measures the association, reproducing base R stats::cor.test(method='kendall') AND scipy.stats.kendalltau BIT-FOR-BIT. tau-b = 0.368, z = 6.85, p ~ 7.2e-12; on the same data Pearson r = 0.335 and Spearman rho = 0.532, so the relation is more monotonic than linear -- which is why a rank correlation is preferred.

claims.statement: Kendall's tau-b of eyes-closed-foam sway vs TMT-A processing speed
-log10(two-sided p): the cognitive-motor association is highly significant
normal-approximation z-statistic of the tau-b test
the association is positive (slower TMT-A -> more sway)
Pearson r on the same data (context: linear correlation)
Spearman rho on the same data (the rank-correlation trio agrees, monotonic > linear)
subjects with both sway and TMT-A (complete pairs)

validation.reference: The newly-authored kendallTau op (Kendall's tau-b, concordance-based, tie-corrected, with the normal-approximation p-value) is validated against BOTH scipy.stats.kendalltau AND base R stats::cor.test(method='kendall') on the identical (TMT-A, sway) pairs -- a double reference. All three compute the same tie-corrected tau-b and the same normal-approximation p, and they agree BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0 vs each). The per-subject eyes-closed-foam sway comes from PhysioMoCap::swayMetrics (path_length, certified against Prieto in the sibling sway-posturography-bds case). Pearson r and Spearman rho are reported on the same data for context.
validation.data: REAL -- Santos & Duarte (2016) BDS; Trail Making Test A time vs eyes-closed-foam COP path length, n=158
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) kendallTau reproduces scipy.stats.kendalltau and base R cor.test(method='kendall') bit-for-bit; (2) slower cognitive processing speed tracks more postural sway. HONEST scope: (1) this AUTHORS A NEW OP, kendallTau (Kendall's tau-b, the third rank-correlation method after Pearson's r and Spearman's rho in correlationTest), and reuses the certified swayMetrics op (path_length, validated against Prieto in the sibling sway-posturography-bds case) for the eyes-closed-foam sway; (2) the tau-b statistic AND the normal-approximation p reproduce base R stats::cor.test(method='kendall') AND scipy.stats.kendalltau BIT-FOR-BIT (|diff| = 0 vs each; the same concordance + tie-corrected variance formula in all three); (3) the finding: slower Trail Making Test A time (worse visual attention / processing speed) is associated with MORE eyes-closed-foam sway -- tau-b = 0.368, z = 6.85, p ~ 7.2e-12 (n=158) -- a moderate, highly significant cognitive-motor association; on the same data Pearson r = 0.335 and Spearman rho = 0.532, so the association is more MONOTONIC than linear (both variables are right-skewed), which is exactly why a rank correlation is preferred here; (4) HONEST LIMITS: this is a MARGINAL (unadjusted) association -- age is a shared correlate (older subjects tend to have both slower TMT and more sway), so a partial / age-adjusted analysis is the natural next step to separate a direct cognitive-motor link from age confounding; a cross-sectional ASSOCIATION, NOT causation; one per-subject value; run_simulation = FALSE (deterministic).

open_questions.q: The association is marginal (unadjusted); age is a shared correlate of both slower TMT and more sway, so a partial correlation or multiple regression adjusting for age would separate a direct cognitive-motor link from age confounding. TMT-B (set-shifting) and dual-task paradigms would probe executive control specifically. The single tau-b shown here is the robust first-line rank correlation. Documented, not escalated.
